name: tag_config_import

artifactId.note: the data-plane upload route accepts Project archives only, so a JSON Tag export artifact is always produced by tag_config_export

provider.note: a Tag provider name; '[' and ']' are refused, because the Target identity is the provider-qualified path

path.note: the '/'-separated destination path the document's Tags are created under; empty means the provider root. Empty, '.' and '..' segments are refused, so one Gateway path has exactly one Target identity

preconditionToken.policy: D30 §2: a Tag import takes no Precondition token, and D11's Phase 4 amendment makes the collision policy its concurrency rule instead — 'Abort' is always sent, so an import creates Tags and never overwrites one. A destination that already holds a Tag the document declares is a `conflict` that dispatches nothing, both checked by the Tool against the Gateway before dispatch and refused by the Gateway itself inside the race window.

targetId.form: [<provider>]<path>: the provider-qualified destination the import creates Tags under, in Ignition Tag-path form
targetId.resolution: one Target per call, built from the validated provider and path; the empty path is the provider root, '[<provider>]'
targetId.matchNote: D30 §1/D08: an allowlist entry authorizes its own path and every path below it, but only at a '/' segment boundary — `[default]CI/Imports` covers `[default]CI/Imports` and `[default]CI/Imports/Nested`, and never `[default]CI/Imports2`. The provider qualifier is compared in full, so `[default]` does not reach `[default2]x`, and an entry with no path is the provider root and covers that provider. No other operation is affected: `exact` membership stays the rule for every Target that is not a provider-qualified Tag path.
targetId.denialCodeSource: D30 §7, Tool-scoped; the Phase 3 machinery keeps operation_disabled

reservedTagProviders.rule: D30 §1: the Runtime Target Policy lives in the reserved `IgnitionMCPPolicy` provider (ticket #6's characterized location), and the Runtime plane must not be able to write it. The refusal is a product rule — Jython handler scope is not a security boundary — so this Tool refuses any Target inside that provider with `permission_denied` before the Target allowlist is consulted, exactly as D30 §5 makes a Refused resource type refuse even under `*`. An entry that names the provider outright therefore changes nothing. The comparison is case-insensitive, because a Tag path that differs from the reserved name only in case addresses the same provider, and the audited reason names the reserved provider rather than the caller's spelling.

artifactInput.visibility: the same Mutation principal that owns the artifact, or ignition.admin (D30 §6); anything else answers not_found, exactly as a missing artifact does
artifactInput.validation: the artifact was JSON-validated before it became READY (tag_config_export parses it against an 8 MiB ceiling), and the import side re-reads it under the same byte ceiling and re-parses it, so an unparseable or oversize document fails with nothing dispatched
artifactInput.kindNote: D11/D30: the document is a JSON Tag export, which is exactly the artifact kind tag_config_export publishes. No data-plane ingress can produce one: POST /artifacts accepts project_archive only.

fixedKnobsNote: D30 §4: the caller cannot choose the collision policy. 'Abort' keeps the import inside the Target the deployment allowlisted: it creates Tags only, and one existing Tag refuses the whole import instead of changing it. Existing Tags change only through the Runtime plane's tag_update, with a Tag config fingerprint.
documentRule: The artifact is the Gateway's own JSON Tag export, read the way the Gateway imports it: a node's non-empty `name` is one path segment, `tags` are its children, and the document's own root is part of what it declares — a root that names a Tag (the export of a sub-path) is created under the import path, and a root with no name (a provider-root export) contributes its children only. The bounded re-export is normalized to the same provider-relative namespace: its root is either the provider root (which names nothing) or the node at the import path, and the import path is the prefix either way. `provision.py` records the Gateway's own behaviour for both shapes in every live row (`tagProvider.convention`).
udtRule: D30 §6: Tag CONFIG Mutations reach UDT definitions only through an explicit `_types_` Target. A document that declares Tag paths under `_types_` is therefore refused with invalid_argument unless the import path itself is the `_types_` subtree, which is what makes the Target explicit.

rejectionPolicy.rule: D30 §2: an explicit Gateway rejection is final for this Tool — a 4xx, or a 2xx carrying the Gateway's own refusal. Ignition reports a refused import inside the documented 200 as a failure report (the recorded 8.3.8/8.3.9 answer is `{"failureCount": n, "failures": [...], "successCount": 0}`; the committed OpenAPI documents a list of non-Good QualityCodes). A collision refusal is mapped to `conflict` (D30 §7), any other reported failure to `upstream_error`, and no read-back may turn either into a success: a destination holding the document's Tags may have been imported by another writer.
verificationMaySucceedWhen: the Gateway claimed success (a 2xx reporting zero failures) and the bounded re-export shows every Tag the document declares
rejectionPolicy.partialApplication: a report of some successes and some failures is not a claim and not a refusal: the Gateway did not refuse the call, so the bounded re-export establishes the state, and an import that created only some of the document is recovery_required rather than a success
rejectionPolicy.uninterpretableResponse: a 2xx body this server cannot read is not a claim of success either: the outcome is unresolved, which the executor reports as recovery_required / outcome_unknown, and nothing is replayed. A reported count that is negative or not a number, a `failures` value that is not a list, and a count that disagrees with the failure list it carries are all uninterpretable, so none of them is read as an explicit zero-failure claim
rejectionPolicy.ambiguousAttribution: an ambiguous dispatch (possibly sent with no response, or a 5xx) is reconciled only by the bounded re-export, and a re-export showing the intended Tags never confirms it — another writer may have created the same Tags — so it is outcome_unknown; a re-export showing none of them is not_applied

verification: a bounded re-export of the same provider and path, compared with the Tag paths the document declares, reported as Observed state. The claimed success is confirmed only when the re-export shows every declared Tag; a declared Tag it does not show makes the call recovery_required, whose message names up to five of them.
